name: Hairstyle maxxing

card.summary: Choosing a cut and style to suit your face shape and hair type; cheap and reversible, with research showing hair shapes first impressions.
card.aka: hair maxxing, haircut maxxing, hair halo
card.note: Tight or heavily traction-based styles are associated with traction alopecia in dermatology studies.

quick.overview:
Hairstyle maxxing is the looksmaxxing practice of picking a haircut and styling approach that suits the face, head shape and hair type. Forum members commonly argue that hair adds volume and texture to the face and can frame features, with some calling this a hair halo.

Research in person perception treats hairstyle, clothing and makeup as part of first impressions, though no trial has tested face-shape-matching rules as such.
quick.mechanism: Cut length, volume, fringe and parting change the visible outline of the head and how much forehead and eye area shows. Practitioners also consider hair type and growth pattern, and may use styling products or chemical straightening or waving.
quick.risks: Haircuts are reversible. Dermatology reviews report that tight, tension-heavy styles can cause traction alopecia, and chemical straightening or waving carries its own review literature.

lead: Hairstyle maxxing refers to selecting hair length, cut and styling to improve overall appearance, particularly by matching style to face shape, forehead size and hair type. In forums the topic appears constantly as requests for hairstyle suggestions with photo posts, and members debate how much hair can compensate for other features [1].

A hairstyle is any arrangement of hair, and historically styles have signalled age, status, religion and identity [2]. Choices are commonly described as depending on natural hair type and growth pattern, face and head shape, and personal and cultural factors [2]. A 2023 review argues that dress, including hairstyle, makeup and accessories, influences first impressions and belongs in models of person perception [3].

paras: Hairstyle maxxing covers cut, length, fringe, parting, texture, and styling products. Encyclopedia coverage of hairstyling lists defining factors including hair type, face and head shape, body proportions, self-image and the stylist's judgment [2].

Hairstyles have long carried social meaning: the oldest known depiction of hair styling is braiding on a roughly 30,000-year-old figurine, and styles have marked marital status, class, religion and subculture across eras [2].

A 2023 review in Personality and Social Psychology Review states that clothing, hairstyle, makeup and accessories influence first impressions, and proposes that perceivers use dress to infer social category, cognitive state, status and aesthetics [3]. The review is a theoretical proposal and does not test face-shape-matching rules.

Face-recognition experiments report that hairstyle is an external feature whose importance falls as a face becomes familiar, with internal features such as eyes, nose and mouth becoming more salient [4]. Within-person variation, including hairstyle changes, has been studied in the context of face learning [5].

Dermatology reviews report that traction alopecia affects up to 32 percent of women and 22 percent of high school girls with Afro-textured hair, with risk rising with tight or combined styles [6]. A study of 874 African adults in Cape Town examined the relation between hairdressing practices and scalp disease [7].
Reviews also cover chemical hair straightening and permanent waving, describing the processes and what dermatologists should know about them [8][9].

Threads on looksmax.org include hairstyle-name requests and advice on styles for long faces or tall foreheads [12]. One poster reports that comments on his hair changed as his body fat rose, which he reads as hair only looking good on an already good-looking face [1].

No studies found on matching hairstyle to face shape as an appearance intervention. Related research covers hairstyle in person perception and face recognition [3][4], and the scalp-health literature on traction and chemical styling [6][8][9].

lore.intro: Members treat hair as one of the highest-leverage and cheapest appearance variables, and the topic is a staple of rating and advice threads [1].

claims.claim: A good haircut can frame the face and hide flaws (the 'hair halo').
claims.believers: Posters say hair can help with a tall forehead or other proportions, and some describe good hair as the first thing noticed [12].
claims.experts: A 2023 review reports that hairstyle contributes to first impressions, but no published study has tested whether particular cuts conceal specific facial features [3].

claims.claim: Hairstyle only helps if the underlying face is already attractive.
claims.believers: One poster says people stopped praising his hair when he gained weight, which he reads as hair only helping an already good-looking face [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this interaction.
